neighbours.label: The article ' a' that opens an appositive noun phrase renaming or summing up what came just before it, after a comma, dash or parenthesis ('…to the left, a move that…'), not ' a' in ordinary subject or object position.
fire: The company moved its headquarters to Texas, a decision that angered many workers.
He quit the band after one album, a choice he later regretted.
The town was built on a hill above the harbor, a position that made it easy to defend.
The singer cancelled the final concert – a blow to fans who had travelled for days.
She learned three languages before the age of ten, a feat her teachers still mention.
The bill passed by a single vote, a margin that surprised even its supporters.
They named the ship after his mother, a gesture that moved the whole crew.
The river floods every spring, a pattern that shaped the farming calendar.
quiet: The company moved its headquarters to Texas, which angered many workers.
He quit the band after one album and later regretted it.
The town was built on a hill above the harbor, so it was easy to defend.
The singer cancelled the final concert. Fans who had travelled for days were upset.
She learned three languages before the age of ten, and her teachers still mention it.
The bill passed by a single vote, which surprised even its supporters.
They named the ship after his mother, and the whole crew was moved.
The river floods every spring, and this shaped the farming calendar.

short: appositive ' a' summing up the preceding clause
notes: Probes (fraction of max 75.5): ', a change that surprised' 0.669, ', a location that made it rich' 0.816, '– a weakness that' 0.504, 'twins, a boy and a girl' 0.457, all on ' a'. Ordinary ' a' as object 0.008-0.014, the same clause with ', which surprised' 0.057. Near misses keep the same sentence and replace the appositive with a relative clause or a new sentence.
